# `adi-launcher` — types

> ADI.exe — the Windows launcher: the one thing a person opens. A tray app that brings the stack up, watches it, and opens the control panel. The counterpart of ADI.app on macOS, which holds the same binaries out of sight and does the same three things.

## `src/cli.rs`

### struct `Report`

Codable mirror of what `adi-mono status --json` emits (see `crates/adi-core/src/commands.rs`). Only the fields the tray actually renders; serde ignores the rest, so a new service or action appearing in the core needs no change here.

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Default, Clone, Deserialize)]
pub struct Report {
    #[serde(default)]
    pub any_running: bool,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub services: Vec<Service>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub setup: Setup,
}
```

### struct `Setup`

What still has to happen before `http://app.adi/` resolves. On Windows that is one thing — the NRPT rule — and it is optional: the panel is always reachable on its loopback port.

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Default, Clone, Deserialize)]
pub struct Setup {
    #[serde(default)]
    pub dns_route: bool,
}
```
